clauses.note: Students discuss what respect looks and sounds like during the protocol, contributing ideas about norms, but the norms (respect) are teacher-introduced and defined rather than student-developed; students reflect on applying them but do not generate or co-create the norms themselves, so the 'developing' act is only partially performed.

clauses.clause: Share individual writing with the group
Listen to others as they share their writing
Offer feedback on peers' writing
Respond to feedback received on own writing

verdicts.evidence: 'How will you show respect during our Role-Play protocol?' (I will listen to my partner and not make fun of him or her.)
verdicts.rationale: The standard requires six separable acts: developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing individual writing, listening to others' writing, offering feedback, and responding to feedback. The resource partially meets the norm-development clause: students discuss how to show respect during the Role-Play protocol ("'How will you show respect during our Role-Play protocol?' (I will listen to my partner and not make fun of him or her.)") and reflect on what respect looked and sounded like, but the norm itself is teacher-introduced rather than student-developed. The discuss-texts clause is met: students discuss Summer Sun Risin' by answering text-based questions (e.g., "'What is Pa doing?' (opening the barn door a little bit)"). However, the four writing-related clauses — sharing individual writing, listening to others' writing, offering feedback on peers' writing, and responding to feedback — are entirely absent from this lesson, which contains no student writing activity. With two clauses at least partially met and four not met, the alignment is partial.

clauses.note: Students engage with the text through a close read-aloud and role-play to learn about what the boy and sun do (concepts about sunrise routines/experiences), but the student-quotable moments of learning through interpretation are thin — the close read-aloud guide is referenced but not shown, and the main student acts are describing/acting out rather than explicitly demonstrating new concept learning from text interpretation.

clauses.clause: Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes (C)

verdicts.evidence: 'What is Pa doing?' (opening the barn door a little bit) ... 'What is the boy doing?' (opening the barn door really wide) ... 'What is the sun doing?' (Shining; filling the barn with sunlight)
verdicts.rationale: The standard requires students to explain and learn concepts by interpreting texts (I) and by constructing texts (C). Students interpret the text "Summer Sun Risin'" during the close read-aloud and Mini Language Dive, where they explain what characters and the sun are doing: "'What is Pa doing?' (opening the barn door a little bit) … 'What is the boy doing?' (opening the barn door really wide)." Students also role-play beginning events, deepening understanding of the text's concepts. However, the construction (C) clause is not met — no student writing or text-creation occurs in this lesson; the teacher explicitly states that writing/drawing will happen "in the next lesson." Because the (C) clause is entirely absent, alignment is partial.
